turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics and training-data analogies

**What wins in this p-i-n MAPbI₃ dataset (training targets ≥ ~17%):**

1. **PTAA-based HTLs with fullerene/BCP ETLs and Cu or Ag contacts** — PTAA gives a shallow HOMO well matched to MAPbI₃, low interface recombination, and hydrophobic surfaces that template large grains: C60|BCP / PTAA / Cu → 18.4–19.1 (spin, slot-die, blading); PCBM|C60|BCP / PTAA / Cu → 18.85; PCBM|Bphen / PTAA|PMMA / Al → 19.48.
2. **NiO-c with interface modifiers or plasmonic additions** — Au-np|NiO-c → 20.0; NiO-c|SDBS → 19.04; [BMIM]BF₄-modified PCBM on NiO-c → 21.33.
3. **P3CT-Na HTL with non-fullerene/C60/BCP ETL stacks** — ITCPTC-Th|C60|BCP / P3CT-Na → 18.49; P3CT-Na|PASP → 18.98.

**Scoring the pool against these motifs:**

- **c030** (IDTT2FPDI | PCBM-60 | Bphen / PTAA|PMMA / Al): near-exact match to the 19.48% recipe, with an added PDI interlayer that improves electron extraction/passivation. Expected ≈ 19%.
- **c038** (PCBM-60|PEI / Au-np|NiO-c / Ag): direct analog of the 20.0% plasmonic Au-np|NiO-c device; PEI dipole layer lowers the electron-contact barrier further. Expected ≈ 18–20%.
- **c044** (PCBM-60|BCP / PTAA / Cu): sits exactly between C60|BCP/PTAA/Cu (18.62) and PCBM|C60|BCP/PTAA/Cu (18.85). Expected ≈ 18.5%.
- **c097** (ITCPTC-Se | C60 | BCP / P3CT-Na / Ag): Se-analog of the 18.49% ITCPTC-Th stack; the graded non-fullerene/C60 ETL suppresses interface recombination. Expected ≈ 18.5%.
- **c088** (Willow glass|ITO, C60|BCP / PTAA / Cu, doctor blading): the champion PTAA/Cu combination; scalable blading of C60|BCP/Cu devices gave 18.4, slot-die 19.1. Expected ≈ 18%.

Runners-up considered but ranked lower: c034/c072 (PTAA/Al, ~17–18), c039 (PCBM|TiO₂-c / NiO-c ≈ 17.4 analog), c079 (NiO-c|SY1 ≈ 17.4 analog), c085 (TTC passivation, ~17.5), c009 (C60|BCP/NiO-c ~16–17), c060 (Zr(acac)₄/NiO-np/Au ~17).

Final: c030, c038, c044, c097, c088
